extensions.northStar: The Shanghai Print Shop — every surface behaves like a sheet off a 1930s lithography press in a Chinese bakery quarter: jade-teal ink as a flat ground, cream enamel sign plates screwed onto it, vermillion seals stamped last.

teal.note: Owner-specified. The ground the brand IS. Never carries cream text at readable size.

pine.note: Owner-specified. Sign frames, tram lattice, and the dark ground that legally carries cream body text (4.61:1).

cream.note: Owner-specified. Sign plates, display type, and every surface a food photo sits on.

vermillion.note: Owner-specified. Seals, Chinese characters, primary action. Never a ground for prose and never behind food.

ink.note: Derived. The only text color used on a teal ground (4.87:1). Warmer and greener than black.

display.purpose: Hero and page titles. Prompt 700. Carries the vermillion registration offset.

body.purpose: Prose only. Sarabun 400 at 17px minimum — the primary customer is 43–58.

seal.purpose: Chinese characters on seals and sign plates only. Self-hosted 15-glyph Noto Sans SC subset, 3.7 KB.

shadows.name: plate
shadows.purpose: A cream sign plate screwed to a teal wall. Hard offset is the plate's thickness; soft blur is the room.

shadows.name: seal-press
shadows.purpose: A stamped seal sits INTO the paper, not above it.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: A plate arriving on the page.

motion.name: registration-delay
motion.purpose: The vermillion plate lands a beat after the cream one — a misregistered two-color press.

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: Seal presses down: scale 1.12 to 1, once, on first reveal.

textures.name: press-teal / press-cream / press-pine
textures.purpose: Halftone dot grid plus paper tooth, applied as a background-image on the element itself (never a pseudo-element, to avoid stacking-context bugs). Without it the printed, textured mascot cutout reads as a sticker on flat CSS.

rules: The four spec hexes are binding and must never be eyedropped from the delivered images — those render halftone and sample off-spec (#559381 for the ground).
Cream on teal is 2.48:1 and fails body AND large text. The poster gets away with it at 200px; screens do not. Text on teal is ink.
Food always sits on cream. Teal and vermillion never touch a bao.
The Latin wordmark is an image. Its typeface is unidentified, so setting it in a substitute reads as a brand error.
No text uses opacity to become secondary. Hierarchy is size and weight.
Corners are 2-4px. The radius scale itself is redefined so a stray rounded-2xl cannot betray the world.
Icons are the brand's own marks — seals, sign plates, lattice. Functional glyphs (chevron, close, menu, phone) may stay.
Chinese characters are decorative in a Thai page: aria-hidden, with a Thai label in adjacent text.
dos: Put every food photo on a cream mat with a vermillion keyline.
Grain every teal ground so flat fields and printed assets read as one material.
Use the registration offset on display type — it is the world's native device, not a drop shadow.
Alternate grounds as full-bleed bands: teal, cream, teal, pine.
donts: No rounded-2xl, pill-shaped rectangles, or blurred color blobs.
No lucide Croissant, Wheat, Leaf, Sparkles, Flower2, Cookie, Coffee — the previous brand's voice.
No glass, backdrop-filter, or gradient mesh.
No cream body text on a teal ground.
Don't swap the value tagline and the poster's product list.
openQuestions: The Latin wordmark's typeface is unidentified and unlicensed.
Simplified (铺) vs traditional (舖) for a Yaowarat/Teochew audience.
brands/BRAND.md §13 still describes the previous cream-led identity; this redesign was confirmed for the website only.
